cases.category: Shared particle/word disagreement; seed44 broad code-switch collapse
cases.interpretation: The stable positions are 你 and 有. Uniform already deletes the first in43/44 and never unambiguously matches the second across all seeds. Weighted44 drops a much larger opening span;42/43 total errors improve. Not a new three-seed omission.
The 是 position competes with 叫/other wording. D delta is0/0/0 and total errors improve or tie. A stable D position is not a stable regression.

cases.category: Contraction fragment plus shared recognition failure
cases.interpretation: ll is a fragment of the reference contraction you'll, not an independent word. Uniform already deletes/substitutes it; weighted42/44 lose a larger bilingual span while43 matches uniform. Do not normalize it away or label it a newly omitted word across all seeds.

cases.category: Adjacent lexical alternative and nonunique alignment
cases.interpretation: 这 competes with the surrounding wording; the weighted deletion is not forced in all optimal paths. Only42 has an extra total edit.
为人类 versus 未来 changes nearby substitutions and deletions. Uniform42/44 already share the weighted output; only43 regresses.

inspirations versus inspiration plus so/suoyi involves number and English-Chinese boundary spelling. Alignment is nonunique;42 outputs are identical. No three-seed new acoustic omission is established.

cases.category: Consistent total-error regression without more deletions
cases.interpretation: Total-edit deltas+1/+1/+1, D0/0/0. English intelligent/intelligence wording and the initial Chinese particle differ. The source may contain nonstandard English; it is not silently corrected and acoustic/reference adjudication is pending.

cases.category: Consistent substitutions/repetition errors without more deletions
cases.interpretation: Total-edit deltas+2/+1/+1, D0/0/0. Opening-word substitutions and repeated-copy counts drive the strict error increase; no deletion increase occurs on this clip.
